verdict: Merck's sales rose 5% to $18.1B on Keytruda's continued growth, but profit fell 12% to $5.1B as acquisition-related charges inflated its cost of sales.

segments.name: KEYTRUDA / KEYTRUDA QLEX
segments.note: The world's top-selling cancer immunotherapy, including $830M from the new under-the-skin version, QLEX. One product is 48% of Merck's revenue — the concentration behind its push to diversify.

segments.name: Other pharmaceutical products
segments.note: Everything else for humans: GARDASIL vaccines ($2.0B, +14%), WINREVAIR for pulmonary hypertension ($694M, +93%), diabetes drugs JANUVIA/JANUMET ($380M, -39% on generic pressure), hospital and other products, including the recently acquired OHTUVAYRE.

segments.name: Animal Health
segments.note: Vaccines and medicines for livestock and pets.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Developing the pipeline meant to replace Keytruda when its patents expire later this decade.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling medicines worldwide and running the company.

otherDetail: Other expense, net, of $27M — this year it excludes a $393M gain on equity investments that Merck counts among the items separating GAAP from non-GAAP results.
oneTimers: Cost of sales includes $1,140M of acquisition- and divestiture-related costs and $396M of restructuring — the main reason GAAP EPS fell while sales grew. Non-GAAP EPS, which excludes these and a $393M equity-investment gain, was $2.49.

takeaways.title: Keytruda still carries the company
takeaways.text: Keytruda and its new QLEX version grew 6% to $8.6B — 48% of revenue. The QLEX launch ($830M already) matters: it can extend the franchise as the original's patents near expiry.

takeaways.title: The next generation is arriving
takeaways.text: WINREVAIR nearly doubled to $694M and GARDASIL grew 14% to $2.0B — the products Merck is counting on to soften the eventual Keytruda cliff.

takeaways.title: Deal costs hit GAAP profit
takeaways.text: Net income fell 12% despite 5% sales growth, on $1.5B of acquisition and restructuring charges inside cost of sales. The 8.9% effective tax rate (vs 14.2%) cushioned the fall.

footerNote: Merck does not print gross profit or operating income lines in this summary; both are computed here exactly as its statement foots (sales less cost of sales; then less SG&A, R&D and restructuring). Net income attributable to Merck was $5,065M; consolidated net income was $5,067M.
